blocks.zh: 無菌操作最佳實務
blocks.en: Aseptic Best Practices

blocks.zh: 本章學習目標
blocks.en: Learning Objectives

blocks.zh: 理解 RABS 中 closed-door 與 open-door intervention 均須遵循無菌操作技術的原因與風險差異
blocks.en: Understand why both closed-door and open-door interventions in a RABS must follow aseptic technique, and how their risks differ

blocks.zh: 掌握 intervention 的資格確認（qualification）流程，包括風險評估、AVS 文件化與 APS 納入
blocks.en: Understand the intervention qualification process, including risk assessment, AVS documentation and inclusion in the APS

blocks.zh: 學習 First Air 原則在介入操作設計中的關鍵角色及其受限時的緩解措施
blocks.en: Learn the key role of the First Air principle in intervention design and the mitigations applied when it is compromised

blocks.zh: 了解 RABS 手套不得接觸 critical surfaces 的規範，以及接觸後應採取的措施
blocks.en: Understand the rule that RABS gloves must not contact critical surfaces, and the actions to take after contact

blocks.zh: 認識 open-door intervention 後所需之額外控制措施（消毒、棄置、取樣、EM 監控等）
blocks.en: Understand the additional controls required after an open-door intervention (disinfection, discard, sampling, EM monitoring, etc.)

blocks.zh: 熟悉 intervention 執行的標準化流程：清線、手套穿戴、視覺檢查、無菌工具使用
blocks.en: Become familiar with the standardized intervention workflow: line clearance, glove donning, visual inspection and use of sterile tools

blocks.zh: 掌握 RABS 手套安裝的三種業界方法及其各自的優勢與風險考量
blocks.en: Understand the three industry methods of RABS glove installation and the advantages and risk considerations of each

blocks.zh: 理解 RABS 手套在操作期間的消毒策略與殺孢子劑使用時機
blocks.en: Understand the glove disinfection strategy during operation and when to use sporicidal agents

blocks.zh: Q 9.1 Aseptic Techniques for Closed- and Open-Door Interventions Q 9.1 封閉式與開門介入操作的無菌技術
blocks.en: Q 9.1 Aseptic Techniques for Closed- and Open-Door Interventions

blocks.zh: 原文內容 Original Text
blocks.en: Original Text

blocks.zh: 導師解析 Tutorial Commentary
blocks.en: Tutorial Commentary

blocks.zh: 核心概念解析 Key Concepts
blocks.en: Key Concepts

blocks.zh: Closed-door vs. Open-door Intervention (關門介入 vs. 開門介入)：在 RABS 中，即使門是關閉的，操作人員透過手套進行的介入仍然存在污染風險。PDA 的立場非常明確：不論門是開或關，都必須遵循相同的無菌操作技術。
blocks.en: Closed-door vs. Open-door Intervention: In a RABS, even with the door closed, interventions performed through the gloves still carry a contamination risk. PDA's position is very clear: the same aseptic technique must be followed whether the door is open or closed.

blocks.zh: Qualified Maximum Time Limit (經過資格確認的最長時限)：所有 open-door intervention 都必須設定經過驗證的最長允許時間。這不是隨意訂定的數字，而是透過風險評估、AVS 和 EM 數據所支持的。
blocks.en: Qualified Maximum Time Limit: Every open-door intervention must have a validated maximum allowable time. This is not an arbitrary number; it is supported by risk assessment, AVS and EM data.

blocks.zh: 比喻說明 Analogy
blocks.en: Analogy

blocks.zh: 想像手術室中的無菌操作：即使外科醫師戴著手套（類似 closed-door），他仍必須遵循嚴格的無菌技術，不能因為「有手套保護」就放鬆警覺。而當需要打開器械包（類似 open-door intervention）時，風險更高，所需的控制措施也更多。RABS 的邏輯完全相同 -- 屏障降低風險，但不消除風險。
blocks.en: Think of aseptic operations in an operating room: even when a surgeon wears gloves (similar to a closed-door intervention), strict aseptic technique must still be followed, and vigilance must not relax because "the gloves protect me". When an instrument pack has to be opened (similar to an open-door intervention), the risk is higher and more controls are needed. The logic of a RABS is exactly the same - the barrier reduces risk but does not eliminate it.

blocks.zh: 重點提示 Key Notes
blocks.en: Key Notes

blocks.zh: EU Annex 1 對齊：此建議直接呼應 EU Annex 1 的核心精神 -- CCS 必須涵蓋所有介入操作。文件中特別強調「Disinfection prior to EM should be avoided」，這是因為如果在 EM 取樣前就先消毒，你就無法真正評估介入操作帶來的污染風險。
blocks.en: Alignment with EU Annex 1: This recommendation directly echoes the core spirit of EU Annex 1, that the CCS must cover all interventions. The document specifically stresses that "Disinfection prior to EM should be avoided", because if you disinfect before EM sampling, you can no longer genuinely assess the contamination risk introduced by the intervention.

blocks.zh: 時間記錄的重要性：每次介入必須記錄開始與結束時間。這不僅是 GDocP 要求，更是事後調查異常時的關鍵數據來源。
blocks.en: Importance of time records: The start and end times of every intervention must be recorded. This is not only a GDocP requirement but also a key data source when investigating deviations afterwards.

blocks.zh: 練習思考 Practice Questions
blocks.en: Practice Questions

blocks.zh: 為什麼 PDA 建議在 EM 取樣之前不應先進行消毒？如果先消毒了，對數據解讀會有什麼影響？
blocks.en: Why does PDA recommend that disinfection not be performed before EM sampling? How would prior disinfection affect data interpretation?

blocks.zh: 貴公司目前的 CCS 是否有涵蓋 closed-door intervention 的風險評估？如果沒有，可能有什麼法規風險？
blocks.en: Does your company's current CCS include a risk assessment of closed-door interventions? If not, what regulatory risks might there be?

blocks.zh: 如何設計一個系統來自動記錄 intervention 的持續時間，而不依賴人工記錄？
blocks.en: How would you design a system that records the duration of an intervention automatically, without relying on manual recording?

blocks.zh: Q 9.2 Qualification and Approval of Interventions Q 9.2 介入操作的確效與核准
blocks.en: Q 9.2 Qualification and Approval of Interventions

blocks.zh: Intervention Qualification (介入操作資格確認)：每一個 intervention 在被允許用於日常生產前，都必須經過完整的資格確認流程。PDA 提出了四大風險因子：
blocks.en: Intervention Qualification: Every intervention must go through a complete qualification process before it is permitted in routine production. PDA identifies four major risk factors:

blocks.zh: 持續時間 (Duration)：越長風險越高
blocks.en: Duration: The longer, the higher the risk

blocks.zh: 複雜度 (Complexity)：步驟越多，出錯機率越高
blocks.en: Complexity: The more steps, the higher the chance of error

blocks.zh: 接近度 (Proximity)：離無菌組件越近，污染風險越大
blocks.en: Proximity: The closer to sterile components, the greater the contamination risk

blocks.zh: 人員暴露 (Exposure)：操作人員介入的程度
blocks.en: Exposure: The degree of operator involvement in the intervention

blocks.zh: AVS (Airflow Visualization Study，氣流可視化研究)：所有 qualified intervention 都必須有 AVS 記錄。這不是「做過一次就好」，而是要確保每個 intervention 對 First Air 的影響都被充分理解並文件化。
blocks.en: AVS (Airflow Visualization Study): Every qualified intervention must have an AVS record. This is not a "do it once" activity; the effect of each intervention on First Air must be fully understood and documented.

blocks.zh: 把 intervention qualification 想成飛行員的飛行前檢查清單 (preflight checklist)。飛行員不會因為「飛過很多次」就跳過檢查。同樣地，每個 intervention 都需要一份完整的「飛行計畫」：你要知道會經過哪些風險區域（proximity）、需要多長時間（duration）、有多少步驟（complexity），以及誰會參與（exposure）。只有通過這些審查的 intervention 才能被「核可起飛」用於日常生產。
blocks.en: Think of intervention qualification as a pilot's preflight checklist. A pilot does not skip the checks because "I have flown many times". Likewise, every intervention needs a complete "flight plan": you must know which risk areas it passes through (proximity), how long it takes (duration), how many steps it has (complexity), and who takes part (exposure). Only interventions that pass this review are "cleared for takeoff" in routine production.

blocks.zh: 自動化緩解措施：PDA 特別建議，緩解措施應盡可能自動化。例如，當 First Air 原則因物理限制無法被遵循時，自動棄置受影響的產品比依賴人工判斷更可靠。這符合 EU Annex 1 中「減少人為因素」的精神。
blocks.en: Automated mitigations: PDA specifically recommends that mitigations be automated wherever possible. For example, when the First Air principle cannot be followed because of physical constraints, automatically discarding the affected product is more reliable than relying on manual judgment. This fits the spirit of "reducing the human factor" in EU Annex 1.

blocks.zh: APS 納入：所有 qualified intervention 都必須納入 APS 計畫中進行模擬。這意味著 APS 不僅僅是「充填培養基」，還必須包含對所有已批准介入操作的真實模擬。
blocks.en: Inclusion in the APS: All qualified interventions must be included in the APS plan and simulated. This means the APS is not just "filling media"; it must also include realistic simulation of all approved interventions.

blocks.zh: 實務應用 Practical Application
blocks.en: Practical Application

blocks.zh: CDMO 情境：假設你的 RABS 填充線在換品時需要更換充填針頭（一種常見的 inherent intervention）。你的資格確認檔案應包含：(1) AVS 影片顯示換針時的氣流模式；(2) 風險評估矩陣記載持續時間上限（例如 3 分鐘）；(3) 與最近鄰無菌表面的距離分析；(4) 操作人員的 SOP 與培訓記錄。只有完成這些文件，此 intervention 才能被列入「approved intervention list」。
blocks.en: CDMO scenario: Suppose your RABS filling line needs to change the filling needle at product changeover (a common inherent intervention). Your qualification file should include: (1) AVS video showing the airflow pattern during the needle change; (2) a risk assessment matrix recording the maximum duration (for example, 3 minutes); (3) a distance analysis to the nearest sterile surface; (4) the operator SOP and training records. Only when these documents are complete can the intervention be added to the "approved intervention list".

blocks.zh: 如果一個 intervention 的 AVS 顯示會短暫破壞 First Air，但該 intervention 在機械上無法避免，PDA 建議的緩解方案是什麼？
blocks.en: If the AVS of an intervention shows that it briefly disrupts First Air, but the intervention cannot be avoided mechanically, what mitigation does PDA recommend?

blocks.zh: 為什麼 PDA 強調「mitigations be automated」？人工緩解有什麼風險？
blocks.en: Why does PDA stress that "mitigations be automated"? What are the risks of manual mitigation?

blocks.zh: Q 9.3 Interventions that Disrupt First Air Q 9.3 破壞第一氣流的介入操作
blocks.en: Q 9.3 Interventions that Disrupt First Air

blocks.zh: First Air (初始氣流)：EU Annex 1 定義的 First Air 是指直接從 HEPA 濾器出來、尚未接觸任何表面的單向氣流。它是 Grade A 環境中最純淨的空氣。任何介入操作都不應阻斷 First Air 到達暴露產品或關鍵表面的路徑。
blocks.en: First Air: As defined in EU Annex 1, First Air is unidirectional air that comes directly from the HEPA filter and has not yet contacted any surface. It is the cleanest air in the Grade A environment. No intervention should block the path of First Air to exposed product or critical surfaces.

blocks.zh: 設計優先原則 (Design-First Principle)：PDA 的建議核心在於「設計」-- 手套孔位置、操作動線、工具放置都應在設計階段就考量 First Air 的維護。事後補救永遠不如事前設計。
blocks.en: Design-First Principle: The core of PDA's recommendation is "design": glove port locations, operator movement paths and tool placement should all be designed to preserve First Air at the design stage. Remediation after the fact is never as good as design up front.

blocks.zh: First Air 就像瀑布般從上方傾瀉而下的「空氣簾幕」。暴露的無菌產品就在這道簾幕的保護之下。當你把手（透過 RABS 手套）伸入操作時，就像是在瀑布中插入一塊石頭 -- 你會在石頭下方製造出亂流區域。因此，你必須確保你的「石頭」（手）不會出現在需要保護的物品正上方，或者使用已滅菌的工具來延伸你的操作距離。
blocks.en: First Air is like an "air curtain" cascading down from above like a waterfall. The exposed sterile product sits under the protection of this curtain. When you reach in (through a RABS glove), it is like placing a rock in the waterfall: you create a turbulent zone below the rock. You must therefore make sure your "rock" (the hand) never ends up directly above the items that need protection, or use sterilized tools to extend your reach.

blocks.zh: 三大法規框架對齊：PDA 特別列出了三個法規文件作為 intervention 設計的依據：EU Annex 1、FDA Guidance、以及 PDA PTC-1。這意味著，無論你的產品目標市場在哪裡，intervention 設計都必須同時滿足這三者的要求。對於 CDMO 而言，這一點至關重要，因為同一條產線可能服務於不同法規市場的客戶。
blocks.en: Alignment with three regulatory frameworks: PDA lists three documents as the basis for intervention design: EU Annex 1, the FDA Guidance and PDA PTC-1. This means that, wherever your product is marketed, intervention design must meet the requirements of all three. For a CDMO this is essential, because the same line may serve customers in different regulatory markets.

blocks.zh: 無菌工具的雙重考量：使用無菌工具（如鑷子）可以避免手套直接接觸關鍵表面，但工具本身的設計、放置和使用也不能增加額外風險。工具越多，操作越複雜，掉落或碰撞的機率也越高。
blocks.en: Dual considerations for sterile tools: Sterile tools (such as forceps) can prevent gloves from touching critical surfaces directly, but the design, placement and use of the tools themselves must not add risk. The more tools, the more complex the operation, and the higher the chance of dropping or knocking something.

blocks.zh: 如果 RABS 手套孔的位置正好在充填針上方，你會建議什麼設計改善方案？
blocks.en: If a RABS glove port happens to sit directly above the filling needle, what design improvement would you recommend?

blocks.zh: 在 intervention 設計審查中，如何平衡「使用更多無菌工具以保護 First Air」與「工具增加操作複雜度」之間的矛盾？
blocks.en: In an intervention design review, how do you balance "using more sterile tools to protect First Air" against "tools add operational complexity"?

blocks.zh: EU Annex 1、FDA Guidance 與 PDA PTC-1 在 First Air 的定義上是否完全一致？如果有差異，CDMO 應如何處理？
blocks.en: Are the definitions of First Air in EU Annex 1, the FDA Guidance and PDA PTC-1 completely consistent? If there are differences, how should a CDMO handle them?

blocks.zh: Q 9.4 RABS Glove Contact with Critical Surfaces Q 9.4 RABS 手套與關鍵表面的接觸
blocks.en: Q 9.4 RABS Glove Contact with Critical Surfaces

blocks.zh: Critical Surface (關鍵表面)：PDA 提供了一個非常務實的定義 -- 只有「直接接觸產品或組件」的設備部位才被視為 critical surface。例如充填針的內壁、瓶塞的接觸面等。而塞栓碗的把手和外表面則不屬於 critical surface，可以被手套接觸。
blocks.en: Critical Surface: PDA offers a very pragmatic definition: only the parts of the equipment that directly contact the product or components are considered critical surfaces, for example the inner wall of a filling needle or the contact surfaces of stoppers. The handle and outer surfaces of the stopper bowl are not critical surfaces and may be touched by gloves.

blocks.zh: 「禁止接觸」的明確立場：PDA 在這裡的態度非常堅定 -- RABS 手套不應被允許接觸 critical surfaces。理由很清楚：RABS 手套和其所處的環境並非無菌的（不像 Isolator 內部）。
blocks.en: A clear "no contact" position: PDA is firm here: RABS gloves should not be allowed to contact critical surfaces. The reason is clear: RABS gloves and the environment they are in are not sterile (unlike the inside of an isolator).

blocks.zh: 這就像餐廳的食品安全規範：服務生可以觸碰盤子的邊緣（non-critical surface），但絕對不能用手觸碰食物本身或食物直接接觸的盤面（critical surface）。如果不小心碰到了，該份餐點就必須被丟棄或重新處理。RABS 手套的邏輯完全相同 -- 你可以操作設備的外部，但不能碰到產品直接接觸的表面。
blocks.en: This is like food safety rules in a restaurant: a server may touch the rim of a plate (non-critical surface) but must never touch the food itself or the plate surface in direct contact with the food (critical surface). If accidental contact occurs, that dish must be discarded or reprocessed. RABS gloves follow exactly the same logic: you may handle the outside of the equipment but must not touch surfaces in direct contact with the product.

blocks.zh: RABS vs. Isolator 的關鍵差異：在 Isolator 中，手套處於 Grade A 環境且經過 VPHP 生物淨化，因此手套表面被視為「可控的」。但 RABS 手套雖然在安裝前已滅菌，但在使用過程中暴露於 Grade B 環境風險。這是 RABS 與 Isolator 在操作層面最根本的差異之一。
blocks.en: Key difference between RABS and isolators: In an isolator, the gloves are in a Grade A environment and have been bio-decontaminated with VPHP, so the glove surface is regarded as "controlled". RABS gloves, although sterilized before installation, are exposed to risk from the Grade B environment during use. This is one of the most fundamental operational differences between a RABS and an isolator.

blocks.zh: 必須有書面程序：文件中明確要求建立書面程序 (Written procedures)，涵蓋：(1) 如何避免接觸；(2) 如果不慎接觸了應採取什麼行動。這意味著單純的培訓是不夠的，必須有 SOP。
blocks.en: Written procedures required: The document explicitly requires written procedures covering: (1) how to avoid contact; (2) what action to take if contact occurs inadvertently. This means training alone is not enough; an SOP is required.

blocks.zh: 請列舉三個你的產線上的 critical surfaces 與三個 non-critical surfaces，並說明你是如何區分的。
blocks.en: List three critical surfaces and three non-critical surfaces on your line, and explain how you distinguished them.

blocks.zh: 如果操作人員在 intervention 中不慎以 RABS 手套碰觸了充填針外壁，你的 SOP 應規定什麼處置步驟？
blocks.en: If an operator inadvertently touches the outer wall of a filling needle with a RABS glove during an intervention, what disposition steps should your SOP specify?

blocks.zh: Q 9.5 Post Open-Door Intervention Actions Q 9.5 開門介入操作後的後續措施
blocks.en: Q 9.5 Post Open-Door Intervention Actions

blocks.zh: Approved Intervention List (經批准的介入操作清單)：這是 RABS 操作的核心文件之一。每一個可能需要開門的操作都必須事先被識別、評估、資格確認，並列入此清單。任何不在清單上的 open-door intervention 都不應被執行。
blocks.en: Approved Intervention List: This is one of the core documents of RABS operation. Every operation that might require opening the door must be identified, assessed and qualified in advance, and placed on this list. No open-door intervention that is not on the list should be performed.

blocks.zh: 五大額外控制措施：
blocks.en: Five additional controls:

blocks.zh: 消毒/殺孢子劑處理：針對非產品接觸表面
blocks.en: Disinfection/sporicidal treatment: For non-product-contact surfaces

blocks.zh: 產品棄置：識別並移除可能受影響的單位
blocks.en: Product discard: Identify and remove units that may have been affected

blocks.zh: 無菌樣品採集：依 CCS 需求判斷
blocks.en: Aseptic sample collection: Decided according to CCS requirements

blocks.zh: 文件記錄：完整的介入操作記錄（時間、描述、參與者、棄置數、EM）
blocks.en: Documentation: A complete intervention record (time, description, participants, number discarded, EM)

blocks.zh: 操作人員監控：手套及其他風險部位的即時 EM
blocks.en: Operator monitoring: Real-time EM of gloves and other at-risk body sites

blocks.zh: Open-door intervention 就像是在無塵室中打開了一扇「緊急逃生門」。每次打開這扇門，你都需要執行一套完整的「善後程序」：檢查是否有外物進入（EM 監控）、清潔受影響區域（消毒）、移除可能受損的物品（棄置產品）、記錄事件（文件化），以及確認「大門」已經安全關閉。這不是一個可以省略的流程，就像機場安檢區被突破後，必須清場重新安檢一樣。
blocks.en: An open-door intervention is like opening an "emergency exit door" in a cleanroom. Each time the door is opened, you need to carry out a complete set of "aftermath procedures": check whether anything foreign has entered (EM monitoring), clean the affected area (disinfection), remove items that may have been compromised (discard product), record the event (documentation), and confirm that the "main door" has been closed safely. This process cannot be omitted, just as when an airport security checkpoint is breached, the area must be cleared and re-screened.

blocks.zh: Intervention Alarm System：PDA 建議 door access 應配備「recorded intervention alarms」。這代表 RABS 門的開閉應該與自動化系統連動，一旦開門就觸發警報並自動記錄。這是減少人為疏失的關鍵設計。
blocks.en: Intervention Alarm System: PDA recommends that door access be equipped with "recorded intervention alarms". This means the opening and closing of the RABS door should be linked to an automated system that triggers an alarm and records automatically as soon as the door is opened. This is a key design feature for reducing human error.

blocks.zh: 操作人員 EM 監控範圍：不僅是手套，還包括前臂、胸部、頭部等部位。這反映了 EU Annex 1 對 Grade A/B 操作人員 EM 監控的嚴格要求。
blocks.en: Scope of operator EM monitoring: Not only the gloves, but also the forearms, chest, head and other sites. This reflects the strict EU Annex 1 requirements for EM monitoring of Grade A/B operators.

blocks.zh: CDMO 的棄置策略 (Discard Strategy)：對於 CDMO 而言，每次 open-door intervention 的產品棄置量直接影響批次產出率和成本。建議在設備設計階段就與設備供應商討論自動棄置功能（auto-reject），並在確效時驗證其準確性。自動棄置比人工判斷更可靠，也更容易通過稽核審查。
blocks.en: CDMO discard strategy: For a CDMO, the amount of product discarded after each open-door intervention directly affects batch yield and cost. It is advisable to discuss an automatic discard function (auto-reject) with the equipment supplier at the equipment design stage and to verify its accuracy during validation. Automatic discard is more reliable than manual judgment and is also easier to defend in audits.

blocks.zh: 貴公司的 open-door intervention 後的棄置數量是如何決定的？是基於時間、位置、還是 AVS 結果？
blocks.en: How is the discard quantity after an open-door intervention determined at your company: by time, by location, or by AVS results?

blocks.zh: 如果一次 open-door intervention 超過了 qualified maximum time limit，你會採取什麼額外措施？
blocks.en: If an open-door intervention exceeds the qualified maximum time limit, what additional measures would you take?

blocks.zh: 為什麼 PDA 說「Collection of sterility samples may be taken, if warranted in the CCS」而不是「must be taken」？這給了企業什麼空間？
blocks.en: Why does PDA say "Collection of sterility samples may be taken, if warranted in the CCS" rather than "must be taken"? What latitude does this give companies?

blocks.zh: Q 9.6 How Should Interventions Be Performed? Q 9.6 介入操作應如何執行？
blocks.en: Q 9.6 How Should Interventions Be Performed?

blocks.zh: Intervention 標準流程 (Standard Intervention Workflow)：PDA 描述了一個非常明確的 7 步驟流程：
blocks.en: Standard Intervention Workflow: PDA describes a very clear 7-step workflow:

blocks.zh: 清線 (Line Clearance)：移除所有產品和空容器
blocks.en: Line Clearance: Remove all product and empty containers

blocks.zh: 停機 (Stop Filler)：停止充填流程
blocks.en: Stop Filler: Stop the filling process

blocks.zh: 穿戴手套 + 視覺檢查 (Don Glove + Visual Inspection)：緩慢、刻意地穿戴，立即檢查完整性
blocks.en: Don Glove + Visual Inspection: Don slowly and deliberately, and inspect integrity immediately

blocks.zh: 執行介入 (Execute Intervention)：依 SOP，使用無菌工具
blocks.en: Execute Intervention: Follow the SOP, using sterile tools

blocks.zh: 歸位工具 (Return Tool)：放回指定位置
blocks.en: Return Tool: Return it to its designated location

blocks.zh: 第二次視覺檢查 (2nd Visual Inspection)：退出手套前再次檢查
blocks.en: 2nd Visual Inspection: Inspect again before withdrawing from the glove

blocks.zh: 安置手套 + 重啟 (Position Glove + Restart)：確保不觸發光幕
blocks.en: Position Glove + Restart: Ensure the light curtain is not triggered

blocks.zh: Light Curtain (光幕)：這是 RABS 中常見的安全/監控設備，用於偵測手套或物體是否侵入特定區域。操作完成後，手套必須被正確安置，避免誤觸發光幕導致不必要的警報或停機。
blocks.en: Light Curtain: A safety/monitoring device commonly used in RABS to detect whether a glove or object has entered a defined area. After the operation, the glove must be positioned correctly to avoid falsely triggering the light curtain, which would cause unnecessary alarms or stoppages.

blocks.zh: 雙人操作制度 (Primary + Secondary Operator)：開門介入必須採用團隊合作模式。Primary operator 負責 Grade A 區域內的操作；secondary operator 在外部協助，確保 primary operator 的手套不會接觸暴露於外部環境的表面。這類似於手術室的「術者 + 遞械護理師」的配合模式。
blocks.en: Two-person operation (Primary + Secondary Operator): Open-door interventions must be carried out as a team. The primary operator performs the work inside the Grade A area; the secondary operator assists from outside and ensures that the primary operator's gloves do not touch surfaces exposed to the external environment. This is similar to the "surgeon + scrub nurse" teamwork in an operating room.

blocks.zh: Intervention 的執行流程就像外科手術的「刷手上台」程序。你不會直接衝進手術室開始動刀。你必須先完成刷手（穿戴手套 + 檢查）、確認手術區域已清場（清線）、使用滅菌器械操作（無菌工具）、操作完成後逐一確認（第二次檢查），最後安全退出。每一步都有其存在的理由，跳過任何一步都會增加感染風險。
blocks.en: The intervention workflow is like the "scrub-in" procedure before surgery. You do not rush into the operating room and start cutting. You must first scrub (don gloves + inspect), confirm the surgical field has been cleared (line clearance), operate with sterilized instruments (sterile tools), check everything one by one when finished (second inspection), and finally withdraw safely. Every step exists for a reason, and skipping any one of them increases infection risk.

blocks.zh: 為什麼 PDA 要求手套穿戴必須「slow and deliberate」？如果操作人員趕時間快速穿戴，可能會有什麼風險？
blocks.en: Why does PDA require glove donning to be "slow and deliberate"? What risks might arise if an operator rushes and dons gloves quickly?

blocks.zh: PDA 為什麼要求介入前後各做一次手套視覺檢查？如果只在介入後檢查，可能會錯過什麼？
blocks.en: Why does PDA require a visual glove inspection both before and after the intervention? What might be missed if the inspection is done only after the intervention?

blocks.zh: 在你的產線中，primary operator 和 secondary operator 的角色和責任是否有明確的書面定義？
blocks.en: On your line, are the roles and responsibilities of the primary operator and secondary operator clearly defined in writing?

blocks.zh: Q 9.7 RABS Glove Installation Methods Q 9.7 RABS 手套安裝方法
blocks.en: Q 9.7 RABS Glove Installation Methods

blocks.zh: 手套安裝就像是在「無菌的氣泡」中進行一場精密的換裝。想像你要在一間無塵室中更換一雙無菌手套，但你的手本身不能碰到手套的外表面，手套也不能碰到房間裡的任何東西。解決方案是：手套被裝在一個密封袋中（像是密封的禮物包裝），你透過手套孔把它送進去，然後用無菌工具打開包裝，再把包裝從另一個出口取出 -- 全程手套都在「保護泡泡」裡。
blocks.en: Glove installation is like a delicate change of clothes inside a "sterile bubble". Imagine changing to a pair of sterile gloves in a cleanroom, where your hands must not touch the outer surface of the glove and the glove must not touch anything in the room. The solution: the glove is packed in a sealed bag (like sealed gift wrapping), you pass it in through the glove port, open the packaging with sterile tools, and then remove the packaging through another opening - the glove stays inside the "protective bubble" throughout.

blocks.zh: 「Inverted」手套的意義：三種方法都提到手套要保持「inverted（反轉/內翻）」狀態。這是一個關鍵的無菌保護策略 -- 手套的無菌外表面（將來接觸 Grade A 環境的面）在安裝過程中是朝內的，從而避免被污染。
blocks.en: Meaning of "Inverted" gloves: All three methods require the glove to remain "inverted" (turned inside out). This is a key sterile protection strategy: the sterile outer surface of the glove (the side that will later contact the Grade A environment) faces inward during installation, which prevents it from being contaminated.

blocks.zh: 安裝時機的建議：PDA 建議在 setup 階段最後一個 open-door intervention 完成後再安裝手套。這樣可以避免剛安裝好的無菌手套在後續的開門操作中被污染。
blocks.en: Timing of installation: PDA recommends installing the gloves after the last open-door intervention of the setup phase is complete. This prevents freshly installed sterile gloves from being contaminated during later open-door operations.

blocks.zh: oRABS vs. cRABS 的差異：Approach 1 和 2 都提到手套包裝可以從 RABS 門下方的開口取出（適用於 oRABS），但 cRABS 需要使用其他方法。這是因為 cRABS 的門在操作期間不會開啟，沒有下方開口可用。
blocks.en: oRABS vs. cRABS differences: Approaches 1 and 2 both mention that the glove packaging can be removed through the opening under the RABS door (applicable to oRABS), but a cRABS needs another method. This is because the door of a cRABS is not opened during operation, so there is no opening underneath.

blocks.zh: 滅菌方式的選擇：文件提到手套可以透過高壓滅菌 (autoclave) 或伽馬射線照射 (gamma-irradiation) 進行滅菌。對於 CDMO 而言，gamma-irradiation 的手套通常以即用型 (RTU) 形式購入，簡化了供應鏈管理。而 autoclave 則需要企業自行管理滅菌確效、裝載模式和參數控制。選擇哪種方式應基於產能規模、更換頻率和總擁有成本 (TCO) 來決定。
blocks.en: Choice of sterilization method: The document notes that gloves can be sterilized by autoclave or gamma-irradiation. For a CDMO, gamma-irradiated gloves are usually purchased in ready-to-use (RTU) form, which simplifies supply chain management, whereas autoclaving requires the company to manage sterilization validation, load patterns and parameter control itself. The choice should be based on production scale, replacement frequency and total cost of ownership (TCO).

blocks.zh: 比較三種手套安裝方法，哪一種的污染風險最低？哪一種的操作複雜度最高？為什麼？
blocks.en: Compare the three glove installation methods: which has the lowest contamination risk, and which has the highest operational complexity? Why?

blocks.zh: 為什麼 PDA 建議手套安裝應在 setup 的最後一個 open-door intervention 之後進行？如果先安裝手套再做 setup，會有什麼風險？
blocks.en: Why does PDA recommend installing gloves after the last open-door intervention of setup? What risk arises if gloves are installed before setup is done?

blocks.zh: 如果你的 cRABS 無法使用 Approach 1 中「門下方開口取出包裝」的方式，你會設計什麼替代方案？
blocks.en: If your cRABS cannot use the Approach 1 method of "removing the packaging through the opening under the door", what alternative would you design?

blocks.zh: RABS 手套安裝三法 (Three Approaches)：PDA 提出三種業界通用的手套安裝方法，每種都有特定適用場景：
blocks.en: Three Approaches to RABS Glove Installation: PDA presents three industry-standard glove installation methods, each suited to specific scenarios:

blocks.zh: 兩大安全保證：無論使用哪種方法，最終結果都必須確保手套 (1) 從未暴露於 Grade B 環境，(2) 從未接觸 Grade A 內的任何表面。
blocks.en: Two safety assurances: Whichever method is used, the end result must ensure that the glove (1) has never been exposed to the Grade B environment, and (2) has never touched any surface inside Grade A.

blocks.zh: Q 9.8 Disinfection of RABS Gloves During Operations Q 9.8 操作期間 RABS 手套的消毒
blocks.en: Q 9.8 Disinfection of RABS Gloves During Operations

blocks.zh: 手套消毒策略的核心原則：PDA 的立場非常清楚 -- 正常操作下，RABS 手套不需要殺孢子劑消毒。消毒只有在手套接觸了非滅菌表面時才需要。
blocks.en: Core principle of the glove disinfection strategy: PDA's position is very clear: under normal operation, RABS gloves do not need sporicidal disinfection. Disinfection is needed only when the glove has touched a non-sterile surface.

blocks.zh: Inversion（反轉）的關鍵角色：手套不使用時必須反轉（翻到 RABS 外側），使無菌表面朝內受保護。如果讓手套自然下垂懸掛在 RABS 內部，無菌表面可能接觸到設備的非滅菌表面，造成污染。
blocks.en: The key role of inversion: When not in use, gloves must be inverted (turned out to the outside of the RABS) so that the sterile surface faces inward and is protected. If a glove is left hanging naturally inside the RABS, its sterile surface may touch non-sterile equipment surfaces and become contaminated.

blocks.zh: Wiping vs. Spraying：即使需要消毒，也必須使用擦拭方式，而非噴灑。在 Grade A 環境中噴灑消毒劑會產生液滴和顆粒，反而增加污染風險。
blocks.en: Wiping vs. Spraying: Even when disinfection is needed, it must be done by wiping, not spraying. Spraying disinfectant in a Grade A environment generates droplets and particles, which increases contamination risk.

blocks.zh: 手套反轉的原理就像你脫下橡膠手套時自然將其翻面。當你把手從手套中抽出時，手套會自然從手腕處翻轉，原本在外面（接觸東西的面）變成在裡面被包住。RABS 手套也是這個邏輯 -- 不使用時反轉，讓「乾淨面」被保護在裡面，「可能被污染的面」暴露在外。下次要使用時，再翻回來，乾淨面就又朝外了。
blocks.en: The principle of glove inversion is like turning a rubber glove inside out as you take it off. As you pull your hand out, the glove naturally rolls back from the wrist, and the side that was outside (the side that touched things) ends up inside, enclosed. RABS gloves follow the same logic: when not in use, invert them so the "clean side" is protected inside and the "possibly contaminated side" is exposed outside. When they are needed again, turn them back, and the clean side faces outward once more.

blocks.zh: 「Below Working Level」的風險：PDA 特別指出，當 intervention 涉及工作面以下的設備維修時（例如修理充填設備底部的零件），手套接觸非滅菌表面的風險較高。這是因為工作面以下通常不在 First Air 的直接保護範圍內，且可能有潤滑油、灰塵等污染物。
blocks.en: The risk of "Below Working Level": PDA specifically points out that when an intervention involves equipment repair below the working surface (for example, repairing parts at the bottom of the filling equipment), the risk of the glove touching non-sterile surfaces is higher. This is because the area below the working surface is generally not directly protected by First Air, and may have contaminants such as lubricant and dust.

blocks.zh: 與 Q9.4 和 Q9.5 的交叉引用：如果手套確實發生了污染風險事件，PDA 指引操作人員參照 Q9.4（critical surface 接觸規範）和 Q9.5（open-door intervention 後續措施）的建議來執行緩解措施。這體現了 PDA 文件內部的邏輯一致性。
blocks.en: Cross-references to Q9.4 and Q9.5: If a glove contamination risk event does occur, PDA directs operators to follow the recommendations in Q9.4 (rules on contact with critical surfaces) and Q9.5 (actions after open-door interventions) to carry out mitigation. This reflects the internal logical consistency of the PDA document.

blocks.zh: Campaign 期間的手套管理策略：在長時間的 campaign 生產中（可能持續數天），手套管理是一個持續性的挑戰。建議建立一個手套狀態追蹤系統，記錄每副手套的安裝時間、使用次數、是否曾接觸非滅菌表面，以及是否曾進行消毒。這些數據不僅支持 campaign 期間的決策（例如何時更換手套），也是批次放行審查的關鍵輸入。
blocks.en: Glove management strategy during a campaign: In a long campaign (possibly lasting several days), glove management is an ongoing challenge. It is advisable to set up a glove status tracking system that records, for each pair of gloves, the installation time, the number of uses, whether it has ever touched a non-sterile surface, and whether it has ever been disinfected. These data not only support decisions during the campaign (for example, when to replace gloves) but are also a key input to batch release review.

blocks.zh: 為什麼 PDA 說「spraying disinfectants inside the Grade A RABS during filling should be prevented」？噴灑消毒劑在 Grade A 中會帶來什麼風險？
blocks.en: Why does PDA say "spraying disinfectants inside the Grade A RABS during filling should be prevented"? What risks does spraying disinfectant in Grade A bring?

blocks.zh: 如果操作人員忘記將手套反轉就離開，你會如何評估此事件的風險？需要採取什麼行動？
blocks.en: If an operator forgets to invert the gloves before leaving, how would you assess the risk of this event? What action is needed?

blocks.zh: 在你的 CCS 中，手套消毒的觸發條件是什麼？這些條件是否已經過風險評估和確效？
blocks.en: In your CCS, what are the triggers for glove disinfection? Have these conditions been risk-assessed and validated?

blocks.en: Suggested further reading: If you are building or improving RABS operating procedures, the following three references should be read first:

blocks.en: EU Annex 1 (2022) [Ref 1]: Understand the latest regulatory requirements

blocks.en: PDA TR22 [Ref 15]: Design an APS program that meets regulatory expectations

blocks.en: Pay particular attention to Ref 14 (Gessler et al., 2011) on the risk of glove pinholes - a key reference for understanding the importance of glove integrity testing.

blocks.zh: 本節重點回顧 Section Summary
blocks.en: Section Summary

blocks.zh: 無菌技術一致性 (Q9.1)：不論 closed-door 或 open-door intervention，都必須遵循相同的無菌操作技術。RABS 屏障降低風險，但不消除風險。所有 open-door intervention 需設定 qualified maximum time limit。
blocks.en: Consistency of aseptic technique (Q9.1): The same aseptic technique must be followed for both closed-door and open-door interventions. The RABS barrier reduces risk but does not eliminate it. All open-door interventions need a qualified maximum time limit.

blocks.zh: Intervention 資格確認 (Q9.2)：每個 intervention 須經過風險評估（持續時間、複雜度、接近度、人員暴露），並配備 AVS 文件化記錄。所有 qualified intervention 必須納入 APS 計畫。緩解措施應盡可能自動化。
blocks.en: Intervention qualification (Q9.2): Every intervention must undergo risk assessment (duration, complexity, proximity, personnel exposure) and be documented with AVS records. All qualified interventions must be included in the APS plan. Mitigations should be automated wherever possible.

blocks.zh: First Air 保護 (Q9.3)：Intervention 設計必須避免中斷暴露產品或關鍵表面上方的 First Air。若因物理限制無法避免，須有文件化的風險評估和緩解措施。設計須同時符合 EU Annex 1、FDA Guidance 和 PDA PTC-1。
blocks.en: First Air protection (Q9.3): Intervention design must avoid interrupting First Air over exposed product or critical surfaces. Where physical constraints make this unavoidable, a documented risk assessment and mitigations are required. The design must meet EU Annex 1, the FDA Guidance and PDA PTC-1 at the same time.

blocks.zh: Critical Surface 接觸限制 (Q9.4)：RABS 手套不得接觸 critical surfaces（直接接觸產品或組件的表面）。必須建立書面程序，定義避免接觸的方法和接觸後的處置措施。使用無菌工具是關鍵緩解策略。
blocks.en: Critical surface contact restriction (Q9.4): RABS gloves must not contact critical surfaces (surfaces in direct contact with product or components). Written procedures must define how to avoid contact and what to do after contact. Using sterile tools is a key mitigation strategy.

blocks.zh: Open-Door 後續控制 (Q9.5)：開門介入後需執行五大額外控制措施：消毒、產品棄置、無菌取樣、完整文件記錄（含警報系統）、操作人員 EM 監控。所有 open-door intervention 須列於 approved list。
blocks.en: Post open-door controls (Q9.5): After an open-door intervention, five additional controls apply: disinfection, product discard, aseptic sampling, complete documentation (including the alarm system) and operator EM monitoring. All open-door interventions must be on the approved list.

blocks.zh: Intervention 執行流程 (Q9.6)：標準化七步驟流程：清線 → 停機 → 穿戴手套 + 視覺檢查 → 執行介入 → 歸位工具 → 第二次視覺檢查 → 安置手套 + 重啟。開門介入須採用 primary + secondary operator 雙人制度。
blocks.en: Intervention workflow (Q9.6): A standardized seven-step workflow: line clearance → stop filler → don glove + visual inspection → execute intervention → return tool → second visual inspection → position glove + restart. Open-door interventions must use a primary + secondary operator two-person system.

blocks.zh: 手套安裝三法 (Q9.7)：Approach 1（閉門，glove port 引入）、Approach 2（開門，UDAF 保護下安裝）、Approach 3（閉門，反轉手套直接引入）。所有方法的共同目標：手套從未暴露於 Grade B，從未接觸 Grade A 表面。建議在 setup 最後一個開門步驟後安裝。
blocks.en: Three glove installation methods (Q9.7): Approach 1 (closed door, introduced through the glove port), Approach 2 (open door, installed under UDAF protection), Approach 3 (closed door, inverted glove introduced directly). The shared goal of all methods: the glove is never exposed to Grade B and never touches Grade A surfaces. Installation after the last open-door step of setup is recommended.

blocks.zh: 手套消毒策略 (Q9.8)：正常操作下不需要殺孢子劑消毒。消毒僅在手套接觸非滅菌表面時才需要。手套不使用時必須反轉（inverted）。消毒方式為擦拭，Grade A 內禁止噴灑消毒劑。
blocks.en: Glove disinfection strategy (Q9.8): Sporicidal disinfection is not required under normal operation. Disinfection is needed only when the glove touches a non-sterile surface. Gloves must be inverted when not in use. Disinfection is by wiping; spraying disinfectant inside Grade A is prohibited.
